subject: fennec
reasoning:
I'm planning out a stylized fennec fox model in TypeScript using the SDK, scaling realistic proportions like oversized ears and a bushy tail into meters, keeping the design compact but structurally sound.

Building the joint skeleton...

I'm thinking of building the head with loft stations instead, tapering from skull to muzzle to nose tip using a series of width/height points along the snout.

Now I'm planning the ears as extruded leaf-shaped outlines in a side-facing plane, tilted outward and thin along the depth axis for that fennec-fox look.

Working out the ear base attachment point using the head's local coordinate frame, I'm reasoning through how the sign convention works so the left and right ears mirror correctly using the `s` parameter (where positive is the right side).

I'm defining the ear outline shape for extrusion, with a pointed tip and smoothing, then setting up a paint function that colors the ear tip differently (dark) from the rest of the ear based on the outline's y-coordinate. Now moving on to constructing the eyes as sphere geometry.

For the eye placement, I'm working through the local coordinate system of the head bone, where the numbers represent right/forward/up relative to the bone's orientation, and checking that the head bone is aimed mostly forward with slight upward tilt. I'm calculating where the eyes land in world space given the head joint position and the forward/up offsets, cross-checking against where the muzzle and skull loft stations sit so the eyes end up positioned correctly on the upper skull area.

Rather than hand-calculating positions, I decide it's cleaner to use a surface-snapping approach: get the surface of the skull loft, find the nearest point to an approximate target position, and stick the eye spheres directly onto that hit point with a slight embed. I plan to do the same for the nose, snapping a small sphere to the nearest surface point at the muzzle tip.

Now I'm shaping the body using a loft through stations along the spine instead of a simple sweep, defining rump, hips, mid, chest, and shoulder cross-sections with varying widths and heights, and tying the loft to a bone chain combining the hips and spine joints for deformation.

I'm choosing a sandy countershaded coat for the fennec, light cream belly against a tan back, and applying that as the paint for the body surface. Then I'm working out the leg structure using limb chains with shoulder and hip joints positioned symmetrically, picking segment lengths that keep the total reach within valid bounds so the front and hind legs stretch correctly down to the feet.

Now I'm sorting out the bend directions for each joint — knee forward, hock back for hind legs, elbow back for front legs — and figuring out how many names each limb chain needs since the point count determines whether I need names for just the joints or also the tip.

I'm setting up the leg chains with proper parent attachments to the spine, then sweeping tube geometry over each leg path with thin radii tapering toward dark paws, and considering adding a scaled ellipsoid part at the foot for the fennec's paw shape.

Now I'm defining the bushy fennec tail as a catmull-spline chain with three spans attached to the hips, giving it a radius profile that bulges mid-tail using a sine curve before tapering to a rounded point, with color bands planned for the coat.

I'm then sketching facial details — a cream-shaded underside on the head loft using a normal-based paint function, plus a lighter inner ear color — while deciding to skip whiskers and a more elaborate mask for now.

I'm defining the color palette (sand, cream, dark, nose, tail-tip, ear-inner hex values), and deciding to skip fur-tuft cards and stick geometry on the tail to limit complexity. I consider adding a dark dorsal stripe via a paint callback keyed on position and normal, confirming the paint function receives Vector3-like points so `.x`/`.y` access works, and note I'll mirror features across the left/right side using a sign loop before moving on to the meta export.

Now I'm working out the limb loft stations (width/height at each point along a bone) and ear extrusion geometry, computing how tilting the ear's y-direction vector affects the cross product with x to determine thickness orientation, and figuring out the ear attachment point in head-local coordinates.

I'm defining the ear outline points to get a convex fennec-style silhouette roughly 0.16 tall, then setting up the paint logic to shade the ear outside sandy and tip darker based on height along the shape.

For the eyes, I'm finding the nearest point on the skull surface near the front-side to place a small dark sphere, and considering adding a tiny white highlight sphere offset slightly from the eye hit point for a bit of shine.

For the nose, I'm placing a small sphere at the nearest skull surface point near the front. Now I'm planning the muzzle as a loft with stations tapering from the skull width down to a narrow nose tip, and considering whether the skull should be its own separate loft with a station at the back of the head.

I'm working out the head joint hierarchy next: a neck chain of two or three points leading up from the body, with the head joint positioned at the end of the neck and the head loft rigidly bound to that single joint. Then I'm thinking through the body loft, which uses a spine chain curving from the hips up toward the neck base.

I'm restructuring the spine so it has three named joints ending in a "chest" tip, making the neck's parent cleanly attach to that chest joint rather than an ambiguous mid-spine point.

Now I'm working out the neck and head chain, adding a separate jaw joint parented to the head so the mouth can open, and lofting both an upper muzzle piece and a lower jaw piece with cream coloring to form the mouth geometry.

For the tail, I'm setting up a three-segment catmull-rom chain parented at the hips, then sweeping the tail with a radius function that tapers from thicker at the base to a sine-based curve, giving it a natural narrowing shape toward the tip.

Now I'm working on leg placement, checking hip and shoulder joint positions relative to the body loft so they emerge correctly from the torso. For the hind legs I'm computing hip, knee, and hock positions using a limb function with segment lengths and bend directions—knee bending forward, hock bending backward—to get a fennec-like leg posture, and starting to define the foot target position.

Working out leg naming and side suffixes, sweeping the geometry with coat and dark colors, and placing a paw sphere at each foot joint using the computed target positions.

Deciding against adding extra fur tufts or cheek fluff for simplicity, then focusing on ear placement relative to the head's local coordinate frame, computing the ear base and tip positions from the skull loft station dimensions and the head joint height.

Checking total silhouette height against ear tips, then placing symmetric eyes using nearest-surface lookup against the skull loft so they sit correctly on the cranium sides. Working out the coat paint logic: using normal and position thresholds to split cream muzzle/belly tones from sand elsewhere, and considering using a countershade helper for the body with a negative level to darken the back relative to the belly, while double-checking the loft function's station and bone parameter options for the head/muzzle shape.

Setting up ears and lower jaw as separate bone-driven extrudes/lofts with their own paint functions splitting dark tips from sand bases, verifying bevel-to-thickness ratios are valid, and starting to write the actual module imports and color constant definitions for the fox model.

Defining the builder, hip joint, and spine chain with catmull interpolation across the body points, making sure the chain's name list matches the number of segments plus the tip so the chest bone resolves correctly.

Setting up the neck chain parented to the chest, then the head joint aimed forward from the final neck segment, followed by a jaw joint positioned and aimed using local offsets from the head.

Building the body loft with station radii from hips through the shoulders, bound to the hip/spine bones.

Now I'm constructing the head loft into a skull surface, then starting the leg generation loop, computing shoulder and foot positions per side and building the foreleg chain parented to the chest.

Doing the same for hind legs, defining hip/knee/hock/foot positions and chaining them to the hips bone with alternating bend directions.

I'm checking that limb lengths exceed the actual joint-to-foot distances so the IK chains stay stretched properly, for both front and hind legs.

Now I'm sweeping the leg bones with appropriate radii, using a paint function to add dark "socks" below a height threshold while keeping the rest coat-colored, then adding scaled sphere paws bound to each foot bone with a slight forward offset.

For the tail, I'm building a curved chain through several control points, then sweeping it with a tapering radius that follows a sine profile and transitions from the body coat color to a dark tip using banded coloring.

For ears, I'm extruding a bone-anchored outline shape positioned relative to the head frame, shaded with a conditional paint that darkens the inner edge. For eyes, I'm placing small sphere geometries at nearest-surface points on the skull mesh, embedding a dark iris sphere and a smaller white highlight offset slightly along the surface normal — though I'm noticing the highlight offset should follow the surface tangent rather than push outward along the normal.

I'm correcting the highlight placement so it sits properly offset along the surface rather than floating off the eye, then working through embed math to confirm the eye and highlight spheres protrude the right amount from the skull surface. I'm placing the nose sphere similarly at the nearest skull point near the snout tip, and lofting a small jaw shape rigged to the jaw bone behind the joint.

I'm deciding to skip whiskers and a cheek ruff for simplicity, finalizing the ear outline extrusion, and preparing the closing export statement along with the needed imports from the builder library. I'm double-checking head coloring with a conditional paint function based on normal and position, verifying spine chain naming across the catmull-rom path, and confirming tail and leg placements sit correctly relative to the ground before writing out the final code block with a brief explanatory note.
